tools.name: Batch delete Gmail messages
tools.description: Permanently deletes multiple Gmail messages by ID, bypassing Trash. A successful request does not confirm individual messages existed or were deleted.

inputs.name: userId
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: messageIds
inputs.about: List of Gmail message IDs to delete. Each ID must be a hexadecimal string (e.g., '18c5f5d1a2b3c4d5'). Obtain IDs from actions like GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS or GMAIL_LIST_THREADS - do not use human-readable descriptions.

tools.name: Batch modify Gmail messages
tools.description: Adds or removes labels on up to 1,000 Gmail messages in one request, supporting operations such as archiving and marking messages read or unread. A successful response confirms request acceptance, not individual message status.

inputs.name: userId
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: messageIds
inputs.about: List of message IDs to modify. Maximum 1,000 message IDs per request. Get message IDs from GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS or GMAIL_LIST_THREADS actions. Accepts 'messageIds', 'ids', or 'message_ids' as the parameter name.

inputs.name: addLabelIds
inputs.about: List of label IDs to add to the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, DRAFT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD, CATEGORY_PERSONAL, CATEGORY_SOCIAL, CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS, CATEGORY_UPDATES, CATEGORY_FORUMS. Custom labels MUST

inputs.name: removeLabelIds
inputs.about: List of label IDs to remove from the messages. IMPORTANT: Use label IDs, NOT label display names. System labels use their name as ID: INBOX, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SENT, SPAM, TRASH, UNREAD. tools.name: Create email draft
tools.description: Creates a Gmail draft with optional recipients, subject, plain or HTML body, attachments, and threading. When a requested thread cannot be fetched, the draft is created without threading; a provided subject is used instead of the thread subject.

inputs.name: cc
inputs.about: Carbon Copy (CC) recipients' email addresses. Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'John Doe <user@example.com>'). Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Optional for drafts (recipients can be added later before sending).

inputs.name: bcc
inputs.about: Blind Carbon Copy (BCC) recipients' email addresses. Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'Bob Jones <user@example.com>'). Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Optional for drafts (recipients can be added later before sending).

inputs.name: body
inputs.about: Email body content (plain text or HTML); `is_html` must be True if HTML. Optional - drafts can be created without a body and edited later before sending. Can also be provided as 'message_body'.

inputs.name: is_html
inputs.about:
Set to True if `body` is already formatted HTML. When False, plain text newlines are auto-converted to
tags. Both modes result in HTML email; this flag controls whether the body content is treated as raw HTML or plain text that gets HTML formatting applied.

inputs.name: subject
inputs.about: Email subject line. Optional - drafts can be created without a subject and edited later before sending. When creating a draft reply to an existing thread (thread_id provided), leave this empty to stay in the same thread. Setting a subject will create a NEW thread instead.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: thread_id
inputs.about: ID of an existing Gmail thread to reply to; omit for new thread. If the thread ID is invalid or inaccessible, the draft will be created as a new thread instead of failing.

inputs.name: attachment
inputs.about: File(s) to attach to the email. Accepts a single file or a list of files. Total message size including base64-encoded attachments must be under 25 MB; use shareable links (e.g., Google Drive) for larger files.

inputs.name: recipient_email
inputs.about: Primary recipient's email address. Must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com') or display name format (e.g., 'John Doe <user@example.com>'). A plain name without an email address (e.g., 'John Doe') is NOT valid - the '@' symbol and domain are required. Optional for drafts (recipients ca

inputs.name: extra_recipients
inputs.about: Additional 'To' recipients' email addresses (not Cc or Bcc). Each must be a valid email address (e.g., 'user@example.com'), display name format (e.g., 'Jane Doe <user@example.com>'), or 'me' for the authenticated user. Plain names without email addresses are NOT valid. Should only be used if recipie

inputs.name: include_signature
inputs.about: Append the sender's Gmail signature (the 'Send mail as' signature configured in Gmail settings) to the message body, ahead of any quoted or forwarded content. Skipped when the body already ends with that signature, when no signature is configured, or when the connection lacks permission to read Gmai

tools.name: Create Gmail filter
tools.description: Tool to create a new Gmail filter with specified criteria and actions. Use when the user wants to automatically organize incoming messages based on sender, subject, size, or other criteria. Note: you can only create a maximum of 1,000 filters per account.

inputs.name: action
inputs.about: REQUIRED. Action that the filter will perform on messages matching the criteria. At least one action field must be specified.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user for whom the filter will be created.

inputs.name: criteria
inputs.about: REQUIRED. Message matching criteria that determines which messages the filter will apply to. At least one criteria field must be specified.

tools.name: Create label
tools.description: Creates a Gmail label and returns its label ID. For nested labels, it may create missing parent labels; on a name conflict it attempts to return the existing matching label.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The email address of the user in whose account the label will be created.

inputs.name: label_name
inputs.about: REQUIRED. The name for the new label. Must be unique within the account, non-blank, maximum length 225 characters, cannot contain commas (','), not only whitespace, and must not be a reserved system label. Reserved English system labels include: Inbox, Starred, Important, Sent, Draft, Drafts, Spam,

inputs.name: text_color
inputs.about: Text color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmail pale

inputs.name: background_color
inputs.about: Background color for the label. Gmail only accepts colors from a predefined palette of 102 specific hex values. Common color names like 'YELLOW', 'RED', 'BLUE', 'GREEN', 'ORANGE', 'PURPLE', 'PINK' are automatically mapped to the closest Gmail palette color. Provide either a common color name, a Gmai

inputs.name: label_list_visibility
inputs.about: Controls how the label is displayed in the label list in the Gmail sidebar. Valid values: 'labelShow' (always show), 'labelShowIfUnread' (show only if unread messages), 'labelHide' (hide from list).

inputs.name: message_list_visibility
inputs.about: Controls how messages with this label are displayed in the message list. Valid values: 'show' or 'hide'. Note: These values are different from label_list_visibility - do NOT use 'labelShow' or 'labelHide' here.

tools.name: Delete Draft
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific Gmail draft using its ID with no recovery possible; verify the correct `draft_id` and obtain explicit user confirmation before calling. Ensure the draft exists and the user has necessary permissions for the given `user_id`.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user; 'me' is recommended.

inputs.name: draft_id
inputs.about: Immutable ID of the draft to delete. Must be obtained from GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS or GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT actions. Draft IDs typically have an 'r' prefix (e.g., 'r-1234567890' or 'r1234567890'). Draft IDs differ from message IDs used in GMAIL_BATCH_DELETE_MESSAGES — do not interchange. When multiple

tools.name: Delete Gmail filter
tools.description: Tool to permanently delete a Gmail filter by its ID. Use when you need to remove an existing email filtering rule.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: filter_id
inputs.about: The ID of the filter to be deleted. Filter IDs can be obtained from GMAIL_LIST_FILTERS action.

tools.name: Delete label from account (permanent)
tools.description: Permanently DELETES a user-created Gmail label from the account (not from a message). WARNING: This action DELETES the label definition itself, removing it from all messages. System labels (INBOX, SENT, UNREAD, etc.) cannot be deleted. To add/remove labels from specific messages, use GMAIL_ADD_LABEL_TO_EMAIL action instead.

inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: label_id

tools.name: Delete message
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific email message by its ID from a Gmail mailbox; for `user_id`, use 'me' for the authenticated user or an email address to which the authenticated user has delegated access.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address. The special value 'me' refers to the authenticated user.

inputs.name: message_id
inputs.about: Identifier of the email message to delete.

tools.name: Delete thread
tools.description: Tool to immediately and permanently delete a specified thread and all its messages. This operation cannot be undone. Use threads.trash instead for reversible deletion.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: ID of the Thread to delete.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address. The special value 'me' refers to the authenticated user.

tools.name: Fetch emails
tools.description: Lists Gmail messages with query and label filtering, pagination, and optional message details. Individual detail fetches returning 404, 429, or 503 are skipped, so a page can contain fewer messages than the list result.

inputs.name: query
inputs.about: Gmail advanced search query (e.g., 'from:user subject:meeting'). Supported operators: 'from:', 'to:', 'subject:', 'label:', 'has:', 'is:', 'in:', 'category:', 'after:YYYY/MM/DD', 'before:YYYY/MM/DD', AND/OR/NOT. IMPORTANT - 'is:' vs 'label:' usage: Use 'is:' for special mail states: is:snoozed, is:u

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user. Non-'me' addresses require domain-level delegation; without it, authentication or not-found errors result.

inputs.name: verbose
inputs.about: If false, uses optimized concurrent metadata fetching for faster performance (~75% improvement). If true, uses standard detailed message fetching. When false, only essential fields (subject, sender, recipient, time, labels) are guaranteed. Body content and attachment details require verbose=true eve

inputs.name: ids_only
inputs.about: If true, only returns message IDs from the list API without fetching individual message details. Fastest option for getting just message IDs and thread IDs.

inputs.name: label_ids
inputs.about: Filter by label IDs; only messages with all specified labels are returned (AND logic). Optional - omit or use empty list to fetch all messages without label filtering. System label IDs: 'INBOX', 'SPAM', 'TRASH', 'UNREAD', 'STARRED', 'IMPORTANT', 'CATEGORY_PRIMARY' (alias 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL'), 'CATEG

inputs.name: page_token
inputs.about: Token for retrieving a specific page, obtained from a previous response's `nextPageToken`. Must be a valid opaque token string from a previous API response. Do not pass arbitrary values. Omit for the first page. Loop calls using nextPageToken until it is absent to avoid silently missing messages. re

inputs.name: max_results
inputs.about: Maximum number of messages to retrieve per page. Default of 1 retrieves only a single message; set higher for practical use. Hard cap is 500 per page.

inputs.name: include_payload
inputs.about: Set to true to include full message payload (headers, body, attachments); false for metadata only. payload may still be null even when true; use GMAIL_FETCH_MESSAGE_BY_MESSAGE_ID for guaranteed complete content. When payload is present, bodies are base64url-encoded in payload.parts; replace '-'→'+'

inputs.name: include_spam_trash
inputs.about: Set to true to include messages from 'SPAM' and 'TRASH'.

tools.description: Fetches a Gmail message by its message ID in the requested format and returns formatted message details. Available fields depend on the format.

'metadata': headers and message metadata without body content - ideal for summarization, analysis, or when you only need subject/sender/timestamp (recommended for most use cases). 'full': complete MIME structure with 50+ h

inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: user_id

tools.name: Forward email message
tools.description: Forwards an existing Gmail message to specified recipients, with optional additional text. The tool copies original message parts into a new message, but may alter MIME structure and attachment metadata.

inputs.name: cc
inputs.about: List of email addresses to CC.

inputs.name: bcc
inputs.about: List of email addresses to BCC.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: User's email address or 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.about: Gmail message ID (hexadecimal string, e.g., '17f45ec49a9c3f1b'). Must contain only hex characters [0-9a-fA-F]. Obtain this from actions like 'List Messages' or 'Fetch Emails'.

inputs.name: recipients
inputs.about: List of email addresses to forward the message to.

inputs.name: additional_text
inputs.about: Optional additional text to include before the forwarded content.

inputs.name: include_signature

inputs.about: Desired filename for the downloaded attachment. This is a required string field - do not pass null.

tools.name: Get Auto-Forwarding Settings
tools.description: Tool to get the auto-forwarding setting for the specified account. Use when you need to retrieve the current auto-forwarding configuration including enabled status, forwarding email address, and message disposition.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

tools.name: Get contacts
tools.description: Lists saved Google contacts with selectable fields and pagination, optionally including Other Contacts. Other Contacts are fetched on the first page; endpoint failures can result in partial results, and contact records may be sparse.

inputs.name: page_token
inputs.about: Token to retrieve a specific page of results, obtained from 'nextPageToken' in a previous response. Repeat calls with each successive `nextPageToken` until it is absent — stopping early silently omits contacts.

inputs.name: person_fields
inputs.about: Comma-separated person fields to retrieve for each contact (e.g., 'names,emailAddresses').

inputs.name: resource_name
inputs.about: Identifier for the person resource whose connections are listed; use 'people/me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.name: include_other_contacts
inputs.about: Include 'Other Contacts' (interacted with but not explicitly saved) in addition to regular contacts. tools.name: Get Draft
tools.description: Retrieves a single Gmail draft by its ID. Use this to fetch and inspect draft content before sending via GMAIL_SEND_DRAFT. The format parameter controls the level of detail returned.

inputs.name: format
inputs.about: Format for the draft message: 'minimal' (ID/labels only), 'full' (complete data with parsed payload), 'raw' (base64url-encoded RFC 2822 format), 'metadata' (ID/labels/headers only).

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value `me` can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

inputs.name: draft_id
inputs.about: The ID of the draft to retrieve. Draft IDs are typically alphanumeric strings (e.g., 'r99885592323229922'). Use GMAIL_LIST_DRAFTS to retrieve valid draft IDs.

tools.name: Get Gmail filter
tools.description: Tool to retrieve a specific Gmail filter by its ID. Use when you need to inspect the criteria and actions of an existing filter.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the filter to be fetched.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address or the special value 'me' to indicate the authenticated user.

tools.name: Get label details
tools.description: Gets details for a specified Gmail label. Use this to retrieve label information including name, type, visibility settings, message/thread counts, and color.

inputs.name: id
inputs.about: The ID of the label to retrieve. Can be a system label (e.g., INBOX, SENT, DRAFT, UNREAD, STARRED, SPAM, TRASH) or a user-created label ID (e.g., Label_1, Label_42).

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

tools.name: Get Language Settings
tools.description: Tool to retrieve the language settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to determine the display language preference for the authenticated user or a specific Gmail account.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The email address of the Gmail user whose language settings are to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user.

tools.name: Get People
tools.description: Retrieves a person's details by resource name or lists the authenticated user's Other Contacts, using a field mask to select the information returned. Other Contacts can be paginated and queried using a sync token for changes since a previous sync.

inputs.name: sources
inputs.about: Source types to include when retrieving other contacts. READ_SOURCE_TYPE_CONTACT supports basic fields (emailAddresses, metadata, names, phoneNumbers, photos). inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: The number of 'Other Contacts' to return per page. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true.

inputs.name: page_token
inputs.about: An opaque token from a previous response to retrieve the next page of 'Other Contacts' results. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true and paginating.

inputs.name: sync_token
inputs.about: A token from a previous 'Other Contacts' list call to retrieve only changes since the last sync; leave empty for an initial full sync. Applicable only when `other_contacts` is true.

inputs.name: person_fields
inputs.about: A comma-separated field mask to restrict which fields on the person (or persons) are returned. Consult the Google People API documentation for a comprehensive list of valid fields. inputs.name: resource_name
inputs.about: Resource name identifying the person for whom to retrieve information (like the authenticated user or a specific contact). Used only when `other_contacts` is false. Deleted or stale resource_names may return partial records with missing `emailAddresses`, `names`, or other fields.

inputs.name: other_contacts
inputs.about: If true, retrieves 'Other Contacts' (people interacted with but not explicitly saved), ignoring `resource_name` and enabling pagination/sync. If false, retrieves information for the single person specified by `resource_name`.

tools.name: Get Profile
tools.description: Retrieves Gmail profile information (email address, aggregate messagesTotal/threadsTotal, historyId) for a user. messagesTotal counts individual emails; threadsTotal counts conversations; neither is per-label — use GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS with label filters for label-specific counts. The returned historyId seeds incremental sync via GMAIL_LIST_HISTORY; if historyIdTooOld is returned, rescan with GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS before resuming. Response may be wrapped under a top-level data field; unwrap before reading fields. A successful call confirms mailbox connectivity but not full mailbox access if granted scopes are narrow. Use the returned email address to dynamically identify the authenticated account rather than hard-coding it.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The email address of the Gmail user whose profile is to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user. Prefer 'me' unless explicitly targeting another account; passing a raw email address that does not match the connected account may fail or access the wrong ma

tools.name: Get Vacation Settings
tools.description: Tool to retrieve vacation responder settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to check if out-of-office auto-replies are configured and view their content.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The email address of the Gmail user whose vacation settings are to be retrieved, or the special value 'me' to indicate the currently authenticated user.

tools.name: Import message
tools.description: Tool to import a message into the user's mailbox with standard email delivery scanning and classification. inputs.name: raw
inputs.about: The entire email message in RFC 2822 format, base64url-encoded. This is the raw email message to import into the mailbox.

inputs.name: deleted
inputs.about: Mark the email as permanently deleted (not TRASH) and only visible in Google Vault to a Vault administrator. Only used for Google Workspace accounts.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

inputs.name: never_mark_spam
inputs.about: Ignore the Gmail spam classifier decision and never mark this email as SPAM in the mailbox.

inputs.name: internal_date_source
inputs.about: Source for Gmail's internal date of the message.

inputs.name: process_for_calendar
inputs.about: Process calendar invites in the email and add any extracted meetings to the Google Calendar for this user.

tools.name: Insert message into mailbox
tools.description: Tool to insert a message into the user's mailbox similar to IMAP APPEND. Use when you need to add an email directly to a mailbox bypassing most scanning and classification. This does not send a message.

inputs.name: raw
inputs.about: The entire email message in RFC 2822 formatted and base64url encoded string. This is the raw message content that will be inserted into the mailbox.

inputs.name: deleted
inputs.about: Mark the email as permanently deleted (not TRASH) and only visible in Google Vault to a Vault administrator. Only used for Google Workspace accounts.

inputs.name: user_id
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

inputs.name: internalDateSource
inputs.about: Source for Gmail's internal date of the message.

inputs.name: page_size

inputs.name: page_token

inputs.name: page_size
inputs.about: The number of key pairs to return per page. If not provided, the page size will default to 20 entries.

inputs.name: page_token
inputs.about: Pagination token indicating which page of key pairs to return. Omit to return the first page.

Rapid calls may trigger 403 userRateLimitExceeded or 429 errors; apply exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) before retrying.

inputs.about: User's mailbox ID; use 'me' for the authenticated user.

inputs.about: If true, fetches full draft details including subject, sender, recipient, body, and timestamp. If false, returns only draft IDs (faster). Increases response payload size; tune max_results accordingly. Use verbose=true before destructive operations to confirm draft identity by subject, recipient, and

inputs.name: page_token

tools.name: Update Vacation Settings
tools.description: Tool to update vacation responder settings for a Gmail user. Use when you need to configure out-of-office auto-replies.

inputs.name: userId
inputs.about: The user's email address. The special value 'me' can be used to indicate the authenticated user.

inputs.name: endTime
inputs.about: An optional end time for sending auto-replies (epoch ms). When this is specified, Gmail will automatically reply only to messages that it receives before the end time. If both startTime and endTime are specified, startTime must precede endTime.

inputs.name: startTime
inputs.about: An optional start time for sending auto-replies (epoch ms). When this is specified, Gmail will automatically reply only to messages that it receives after the start time. If both startTime and endTime are specified, startTime must precede endTime.

inputs.name: enableAutoReply
inputs.about: Flag that controls whether Gmail automatically replies to messages.

inputs.name: responseSubject
inputs.about: Optional text to prepend to the subject line in vacation responses. In order to enable auto-replies, either the response subject or the response body must be nonempty.

inputs.name: responseBodyHtml
inputs.about: Response body in HTML format. Gmail will sanitize the HTML before storing it. If both response_body_plain_text and response_body_html are specified, response_body_html will be used.

inputs.name: restrictToDomain
inputs.about: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are outside of the user's domain. This feature is only available for Google Workspace users.

inputs.name: restrictToContacts
inputs.about: Flag that determines whether responses are sent to recipients who are not in the user's list of contacts.

inputs.name: responseBodyPlainText
inputs.about: Response body in plain text format. If both response_body_plain_text and response_body_html are specified, response_body_html will be used.

tools.name: Who Am I
tools.description: Return the identity (email, name) of the connected Gmail account.
